descriptor: HVDC reactors, instrument transformers and grid power electronics
lede: A Sangli maker of reactors and coils for HVDC and grid projects that tripled its revenue in a year by buying control of Mehru (instrument transformers) and Endoks (Turkish power electronics and battery storage). Orders are strong and margins high, but a third of profit belongs to minority partners, a big new plant is late, and the stock trades near 96x earnings.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue ₹1,007 Cr (company figure) against ₹800 Cr guided at the start of the year, at a 23.5% EBITDA margin; Q1 FY27 margin 25% and the order book jumped to ₹1,945 Cr (1.9x revenue). Debt-free with ~₹250 Cr cash at March.

Endoks and Mehru are only 51% owned: ₹186 Cr consolidated profit in FY26, but ~₹121 Cr (EPS ₹15.67) for Quality Power shareholders. Profit swings with Turkish hyperinflation accounting, the Sangli plant has slipped, and another raise of under ₹500 Cr is planned for acquisitions.
~96x trailing earnings and ~69x EV/EBITDA, against 34x for Voltamp, 33x for Transformers & Rectifiers and 118x for Hitachi Energy India.

blocks.text: Quality Power makes air-core reactors, coils and line traps used in HVDC links, FACTS and grid connections, mostly for global OEMs such as Hitachi Energy, Siemens and GE, and exports most of its output. Through 51% stakes it owns Mehru (high-voltage instrument transformers, supplying about one in two used in India) and Endoks in Turkey (STATCOMs, SVCs and now battery-storage power conversion systems). Sukrut (transformer components) is a 50% associate.

items.text: Coil products earn the highest margins: Quality Power EBIT 33% in FY26, orders booked above 25%.
Endoks ~32% EBITDA in Turkish lira terms; battery-storage converters start at 10-12% and should rise to 17-18% with volume.
Mehru 15% EBIT in FY26, guided to ~18%.
IPO in February 2025; revenue from ₹183 Cr (FY22) to ₹947 Cr (FY26, Screener).
Bought 51% of Mehru (March 2025); Endoks consolidated as a 51% step-down subsidiary.
Building a new Sangli coil plant, a CTC magnet-wire line and a PCS factory in Turkey; acquiring Winwin (ex-WS) Insulators at an EV of ~₹315 Cr.

items.text: FY26 EPS ₹15.67 implies ~₹121 Cr for shareholders out of ₹186 Cr consolidated profit; the rest belongs to partners in Endoks and Mehru.
₹240 Cr of operating cash flow against ₹423 Cr of profit over FY22-26; other income (interest, forex) was ₹58 Cr in FY26, about a quarter of pre-tax profit.
borrowings ₹40 Cr against ₹542 Cr of equity; interest cover above 30x.
Capital employed rose ~₹391 Cr from FY24 to FY26 (IPO and acquisitions) and post-tax operating profit rose ~₹118 Cr, before minority shares.

items.text: Promoters (Pandyan family) hold 73.9%, unchanged; no pledge.
Foreign institutions 3.4%, domestic institutions 6.5%; shareholders up to 85,700 from 58,100 a year ago.
Promoters waived dividends and pay rises for a second year ahead of the planned fund-raise.
Auditors flagged contract-asset balances (revenue recognised before billing) as a key audit matter.
Group companies trade with each other (e.g. purchases from a wholly owned projects subsidiary), approved under shareholder limits.
Some Endoks directors own stakes in Inavitas, a related software company.

blocks.text: Its nearest global rivals are Trench (reactors) and Arteche (instrument transformers); Hitachi, Siemens and GE are mostly customers, not competitors.

items.text: HVDC reactors and instrument transformers need years of type tests and customer audits.

items.name: Bull
items.text: Guidance met plus Winwin: revenue ~₹1,800 Cr in FY28, 14% of revenue reaching shareholders after minorities (₹252 Cr), valued at 60x.

items.name: Base
items.text: 20% then ~40% growth to ~₹1,550 Cr, 12.5% to shareholders (₹194 Cr), valued at 50x.

items.name: Bear
items.text: Sangli slow and margins slip: ~₹1,250 Cr revenue, 11% to shareholders (₹138 Cr), valued at 35x.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Management has beaten its own guidance and holds a strong order book in a scarce niche. But the price assumes FY28's 50% growth arrives on time, a big plant ramps smoothly, and acquisitions keep paying off; a third of group profit also goes to minority partners. The margin for error is thin.
